findings.title: Continuous capture advertises 600 segments / 50 min but the server accepts part indexes 0..199 only; any recording that reaches 200 segments is discarded in full at staging
findings.userImpact: A continuous screen recording that runs past ~19.9 minutes at the default 6 s segments (fewer with rotation rollovers) cannot be staged. Segment 200+ uploads fail, backpressure stops recording, and at 'Continue to Finish & Sign' the manifest part is refused, sealDirectCapture discards the session and the reserved record: every already-uploaded segment is released and the local copies were already deleted. The user loses the whole recording.
findings.legalImpact: Destructive loss of an acquisition the user was told was bounded at 50 minutes; nothing is sealed.
findings.reproduction: Start Continuous Capture (continuous-capture.tsx:237 calls startContinuousCapture() with defaults -> segmentMs 6000, maxSegments 600). Record low-motion content (so the 512 MB byte ceiling is not hit first) for > 20 min. Segment sequence 200 -> uploadDirectCaptureItem POST /v1/capture/direct-sessions/:id/parts/200/declaration -> PartParams max(199) (capture-trust.routes.ts:230) / INVALID_PART_INDEX (direct-capture-ingest.service.ts:495) -> retries exhausted -> toast. After 8 failures backpressure stops recording. Stop -> Continue: stageContinuousCapture sets manifestPartIndex = declared.length = 200 (continuous-capture.ts:261) -> declaration refused -> sealDirectCapture catch -> discardDirectCaptureSession (direct-capture.ts:273) -> reservation released; UI says 'nothing was saved'.
findings.observed: Client/native/manifest bound = 600 segments (+1 manifest part) and 50 min; server bound = 200 parts total (indexes 0..199).
findings.expected: One bound shared by native, client, manifest validator and the part writer; recording stops (COMPLETE, BOUNDS_REACHED) before the server limit, with room for the manifest part.
findings.rootCause: SCREEN_CONTINUOUS_STREAM_BOUNDS.maxSegments / SCREEN_CONTINUOUS_MANIFEST_BOUNDS.maxSegments (600) were never reconciled with MAX_EVIDENCE_PARTS (200) introduced by ET-ACQ-07.
findings.remediation: Make MAX_EVIDENCE_PARTS the single authority imported by the shared stream bounds (maxSegments = MAX_EVIDENCE_PARTS - 1) and the native clamp, or raise MAX_EVIDENCE_PARTS for continuous modes; additionally never discard a session whose segments are all verified — stage failure after segments exist should keep the session, not release it.
findings.requiredTests: Integration: open a DIRECT_SCREEN_CAPTURE_ANDROID_CONTINUOUS session, declare partIndex 199 and 200 -> assert the configured maxSegments+1 fits. Shared unit: assert SCREEN_CONTINUOUS_STREAM_BOUNDS.maxSegments + 1 <= MAX_EVIDENCE_PARTS. Mobile: stage with 200 declared segments.
findings.runtimeProbe: In uc3-continuous-capture.integration.test.ts: open a continuous session, reserve, and POST /v1/capture/direct-sessions/:id/parts/200/declaration -> observe 400 while validateScreenContinuousManifest accepts 600 segments.

findings.title: Lost segments are never reconciled against the recorded count: a lost TAIL seals as COMPLETE_SESSION, a lost middle segment discards the whole recording
findings.userImpact: If the network drops near the end of a recording, the final segment(s) fail at the declaration step, the review card shows 'N recorded, M uploaded and ready to seal', and Continue seals the M-segment prefix labelled 'Complete — no known interruption'. If instead a middle segment is lost, the manifest part collides with an existing part index, staging fails and the whole session (all good segments) is discarded.
findings.legalImpact: A truncated recording is sealed and reported as a COMPLETE continuous session: the record claims continuity/completeness over content it does not contain.
findings.reproduction: Record 10 segments; make the declaration POST for sequences 8 and 9 fail (e.g. airplane mode as recording stops). pump().catch only toasts (continuous-capture.tsx:138-145). finalize() drains and calls stageContinuousCapture with declared = 0..7 (no comparison with result.segmentCount = 10). deriveSessionCompleteness returns COMPLETE_SESSION because native said so (continuous-capture.ts:102-107). Manifest has contiguous sequences 0..7, manifest partIndex = 8 (never declared, no collision). Server: sequences contiguous (screen-continuous-manifest.ts:357-362), no gap between listed segments, totalDurationMs <= window (:404) — there is no check that the last segment ends near totalDurationMs or that segments.length equals the recorded count. continuous-complete seals; endReason CONTINUOUS_COMPLETE_SESSION. Middle-loss variant: sequence 4 undeclared -> declared.length = 9 -> manifest partIndex 9 is already declared by segment 9 -> PART_ALREADY_DECLARED -> sealDirectCapture discards everything, with the 'manifest could not be staged' message.
findings.observed: The manifest does not carry the recorded segment count; the client never compares declared vs recorded; the validator's COMPLETE rules do not bound the tail; manifestPartIndex is derived from declared.length.
findings.expected: Before staging, declared.length must equal the native segmentCount or the manifest must be downgraded to INTERRUPTED_SESSION with a limitation; the manifest should state recordedSegmentCount and the server should refuse COMPLETE when segments.length != recordedSegmentCount or when last.startedAtOffsetMs + last.durationMs falls short of totalDurationMs by more than maxGapMs. The manifest part index should be a reserved index (e.g. max(declared partIndex)+1 or a fixed slot), not declared.length.
findings.rootCause: Completeness is taken from the native recorder's termination only; upload-side loss is not an input to completeness, and the server cannot see segments that were never declared.
findings.remediation: Client: in finalize, compare declaredRef.current.length with resultRef.current.segmentCount; retry missing segments from seenRef (files still on disk) and, if still missing, mark INTERRUPTED_SESSION + a new limitation (e.g. SEGMENT_UPLOAD_LOST) and seal the contiguous prefix instead of discarding. Shared: add recordedSegmentCount to the manifest and a tail-coverage check to validateScreenContinuousManifest for COMPLETE. Use max(partIndex)+1 for the manifest part.
findings.requiredTests: Shared: COMPLETE manifest whose last segment ends > maxGapMs before totalDurationMs is refused; COMPLETE with segments.length < recordedSegmentCount refused. Integration: seal with a missing tail -> must be INTERRUPTED or refused. Mobile: finalize with declared < recorded downgrades completeness and keeps the session.
findings.runtimeProbe: uc3-continuous-capture.integration.test.ts: record 3 segments of 6000 ms (totalDurationMs 18000, window 18 s), declare+upload only sequences 0..1 and a COMPLETE_SESSION manifest listing 0..1 with totalDurationMs 18000 -> today it seals (expect CONTINUOUS_COMPLETE_SESSION).

findings.title: POST_NOTIFICATIONS is declared but never requested, so on Android 13+ the 'Capture Frame'/'Stop' notification — UC-2's only way to capture another app — is not shown
findings.userImpact: On a fresh Android 13+ install the notification permission is off by default and PROOVRA never asks for it. The foreground service still runs, but its notification (with the Capture Frame and Stop actions) does not appear in the shade. The screen tells the user to 'open the app you want to capture, then tap Capture Frame from the notification'; the in-app button can only capture PROOVRA itself. UC-2 cannot capture third-party content; UC-3 loses its out-of-app Stop control.
findings.legalImpact: none directly; the primary UC-2 acquisition is unreachable.
findings.reproduction: grep -rn 'POST_NOTIFICATIONS|PermissionsAndroid|expo-notifications|requestPermission' apps/mobile/src apps/mobile/app apps/mobile/modules -> no runtime request exists; package.json has no expo-notifications. Install on Android 13+/targetSdk>=33, start Direct Screen Capture, leave PROOVRA: no notification actions are available.
findings.observed: Manifest-only declaration; no runtime permission request before starting either foreground service.
findings.expected: Request POST_NOTIFICATIONS (PermissionsAndroid.request on API 33+) before startCapture/startContinuousCapture; if denied, disclose that out-of-app Capture Frame/Stop will be unavailable (or refuse UC-2 cross-app mode).
findings.rootCause: Android 13 runtime notification permission was treated as a manifest declaration.
findings.remediation: Add a pre-start permission step in screen-capture.tsx/continuous-capture.tsx (PermissionsAndroid.request('android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS') when Platform.Version >= 33) and a denied-state explanation.
findings.requiredTests: Mobile unit: start() requests the permission on API 33+ before calling the native start. Device acceptance: fresh install on Android 13/14, verify notification actions visible.
findings.runtimeProbe: Device only (Android 13+ emulator, fresh install): start UC-2, check `adb shell dumpsys notification` for NOTIF_ID 0x50D2 posted but suppressed.

findings.title: A continuous recording is not resumable after the JS runtime or process restarts; the native session is orphaned and further segments are silently lost
findings.userImpact: If the Activity/JS context is recreated (app swiped away, OOM kill of the UI, dev reload) while the foreground service keeps recording, the new screen has no sessionRef, so the focus reconnect is skipped, segments emitted by the service are not uploaded, and pressing Start again opens a NEW server session and reserves a new record before native rejects with BUSY. The first recording cannot be recovered; segments accumulate in cacheDir.
findings.legalImpact: Recorded content is lost without a sealed record; the partially uploaded session is only released by the reaper.
findings.reproduction: Session/evidence ids and the declared list live only in React refs (continuous-capture.tsx:88-90); nothing is persisted until finalize's saveCaptureSession (:345). useFocusEffect reconnects only `if (s.active && sessionRef.current)` (:194). getContinuousState returns only {active, segmentCount} (index.ts:223) — there is no native API to re-list finalized segments, and onSegment is a static closure bound to the old module instance (ProovraScreenCaptureModule.kt:124).
findings.observed: Header comment claims it 'reconnects to an in-flight session on return so a new CaptureSession is never created'; that holds only within one JS lifetime.
findings.expected: Persist {captureSessionId, evidenceId, expiresAtUtc, declared segments} as soon as the session opens; expose a native listSegments(); on relaunch reattach to the active native session and resume uploading, or offer an explicit recover/stop-and-discard.
findings.rootCause: Durability of the streaming session was designed around the React component lifetime, not the foreground-service lifetime.
findings.remediation: Persist the session record at start (capture-session-store) and update it per declared segment; add getContinuousSegments() to the Kotlin module; on mount, if native is active, reattach; if a persisted session exists with native inactive, offer resume-upload of on-disk segments or discard (calling discardDirectCaptureSession).
findings.requiredTests: Mobile unit: mount with native active + persisted session -> reattaches, does not open a new session. Device: kill UI during recording, relaunch, continue.
findings.runtimeProbe: Device: start UC-3, `adb shell am kill` is not enough (kills service too) — instead trigger a JS reload in a dev build and observe that segments stop uploading while the notification persists.

findings.title: The staged continuous session is persisted with the expiry returned at OPEN, not the slid server expiry, so Capture drops a long recording as 'stale' while the server session is still live
findings.userImpact: A recording opened at T0 (expiresAtUtc T0+60 min) and staged at ~T0+51 min is saved with expiresAtUtc T0+60 min. If the Capture screen mounts after that (app restart, navigation back later), isSessionResumable is false, the durable record is cleared and the user is told the capture could not be completed — although the server slid the expiry to ~T0+111 min. Local segments were already deleted, so the recording is lost.
findings.legalImpact: Loss of a staged, fully verified-in-place acquisition before it can be sealed.
findings.reproduction: openDirectCaptureSession stores expiresAtUtc from the open response (direct-capture.ts:79-82). Declarations slide the server expiry (direct-capture-ingest.service.ts:588) but the response of declaration is ignored for expiry. saveCaptureSession({ expiresAtUtc: active.session.expiresAtUtc }) (continuous-capture.tsx:348). capture.tsx:491-495: !isSessionResumable -> setStaleRecovered + clearCaptureSession; isSessionStale treats expiresAtUtc <= now as stale (capture-session-store.ts:121-123).
findings.observed: Client-side expiry authority lags the server's sliding expiry by the whole recording duration.
findings.expected: The client stores the current server expiry (return it from declaration/part responses or re-read the session) or asks the server whether the session is still ACTIVE before treating it as stale.
findings.rootCause: ET-DC-06 made the server expiry slide, but the mobile durable record kept the open-time value.
findings.remediation: Return expiresAtUtc from the declaration route and update the in-memory session; or add GET /v1/capture/direct-sessions/:id status and consult it on resume instead of the stored timestamp.
findings.requiredTests: Mobile unit: staging after a slid expiry persists the slid value. Integration: declaration response carries the new expiry.
findings.runtimeProbe: direct-capture-session-sliding-expiry.integration.test.ts already proves the server slides; add an assertion that the declaration response exposes the slid expiry (today it returns only {declaration}).

findings.title: Continuous Discard / Try Again / denied consent never call discardDirectCaptureSession; the opened session and reserved record linger until the reaper
findings.userImpact: The server session and reserved Evidence stay ACTIVE for up to an hour after the user discarded (or after consent was denied); uploaded segment objects remain until the sweep releases them.
findings.legalImpact: none (reserved records are not listed; the reaper releases them).
findings.reproduction: reset() (continuous-capture.tsx:388-396) only deletes local files and clears refs; start()'s catch (:257-263) nulls sessionRef after beginContinuousSession succeeded but startContinuousCapture rejected (PERMISSION_DENIED / BUSY). Contrast direct-capture.ts:251-276 which states every abandoned reservation must be discarded.
findings.observed: No server discard on these paths.
findings.expected: Call discardDirectCaptureSession(session) on Discard, on Try Again from a live session, and when native start fails after the session was opened (or open the session only after consent).
findings.rootCause: sealDirectCapture wraps only the staging step, not the pre-staging lifecycle.
findings.remediation: Wrap start failure and reset() with discardDirectCaptureSession(sessionRef.current.session).catch(()=>{}).
findings.requiredTests: Mobile unit (source-contract like direct-capture-seal.test.mjs): every exit path from an opened continuous session calls discard.

findings.title: Logout / account switch does not stop an active MediaProjection capture and does not clear the (user-unscoped) persisted capture session
findings.userImpact: Signing out while a continuous capture runs leaves the foreground service recording the screen (up to 50 min) into the app cache; uploads fail with no token. The next account on the device is offered the previous user's staged session record (captureSessionId/evidenceId/manifest) on /capture.
findings.legalImpact: Screen content keeps being recorded after the user ended their session; another user's capture metadata is presented on a shared device.
findings.securityImpact: Local cross-account exposure of capture metadata (the server refuses the foreign session, 404).
findings.reproduction: doLogout (settings.tsx:183-188) calls logoutApi, clears tokens and navigates; it calls neither stopContinuousCapture/stopScreenCapture nor clearCaptureSession. STORAGE_KEY is a constant 'proovra.capture.session.v1' with no user id (capture-session-store.ts:24); capture.tsx:487-492 loads and offers it to whoever is signed in.
findings.observed: Capture lifecycle is independent of auth lifecycle.
findings.expected: Logout stops any native capture, discards open direct-capture sessions while the token is still valid, clears local spool and the persisted session; the store is keyed by user id.
findings.rootCause: No logout hook for capture state.
findings.remediation: Add a capture teardown to the logout path (stop native, discard session, delete cache files, clearCaptureSession) and scope STORAGE_KEY per user.
findings.requiredTests: Mobile unit: logout invokes the teardown; store read ignores another user's record.
findings.runtimeProbe: Device: start UC-3, log out, confirm the recording notification persists.

findings.title: A segment whose MediaRecorder.stop() failed is still emitted, uploaded and sealed as an ORIGINAL segment
findings.userImpact: When stop() throws (e.g. a segment stopped almost immediately after start on rotation rollover or Stop, or encoder error), the partially written mp4 (no finalized moov) is still reported with a wall-clock durationMs and becomes part of the sealed evidence; playback/derived intelligence may fail on it while the manifest presents it as recorded video.
findings.legalImpact: A sealed segment may be unplayable while the manifest asserts its duration.
findings.reproduction: finalizeCurrentSegment: `try { r.stop() } catch (_: Throwable) {}` then `if (file != null && file.exists() && file.length() > 0)` emits the segment with durationMs = now - segmentStartMs. No flag is recorded when stop() failed.
findings.observed: Stop failure is swallowed; the file-size check is the only validity test.
findings.expected: If stop() throws, delete the file (or keep it but mark it) and add a limitation / downgrade to INTERRUPTED_SESSION; server-side container sanity check on video segments.
findings.rootCause: Error from MediaRecorder.stop() treated as ignorable.
findings.remediation: Track stopFailed; skip emitting (and record a gap/limitation, which forces INTERRUPTED) or emit with a 'corrupt' flag the manifest must carry.
findings.requiredTests: Kotlin unit/instrumented: stop() throwing -> no segment emitted + limitation. Server: optional mp4 header sanity check.
findings.runtimeProbe: Device: rotate twice within <1 s during UC-3 and inspect emitted segment files with ffprobe.

findings.title: Continuous completeness is written to the session after the seal in a separate statement; a failure there makes an INTERRUPTED recording read as complete downstream
findings.userImpact: Rare: if the process dies or the update fails after completeDirectCapture commits, the session keeps endReason COMPLETED and captureSessionAcquisitionComplete() returns true for an interrupted recording.
findings.legalImpact: Downstream (worker/report) completeness reading can be wrong for an interrupted session.
findings.reproduction: completeDirectCapture sets endReason 'COMPLETED' in its bind claim (direct-capture-ingest.service.ts:856-868); only afterwards continuous-capture.service.ts:185-188 overwrites endReason with continuousEndReasonFor(...). A retry returns alreadyBound early (direct-capture-ingest.service.ts:776-790) but the continuous service still re-runs the update, so a client retry would heal it — only if the client retries.
findings.expected: Pass the completeness into completeDirectCapture so the bind claim writes the final endReason in the same update.
findings.rootCause: ET-DC-09 fix appended a post-seal update instead of threading completeness into the bind.
findings.remediation: Add an optional endReason parameter to completeDirectCapture used by the ACTIVE->BOUND updateMany.
findings.requiredTests: Integration: inject a failure after bind; assert endReason is CONTINUOUS_INTERRUPTED_SESSION.

findings.title: UC-2 still classes the manifest part CAPTURE_MANIFEST after the seal, which ET-DC-11 recorded as removed
findings.userImpact: A sealed UC-2 record's part row is mutated after signing; if the process fails between seal and relabel, the manifest JSON stays classed as an original frame artifact.
findings.legalImpact: Minor: post-seal mutation of part metadata.
findings.reproduction: screen-capture.service.ts: completeDirectCapture (:125) then evidencePart.updateMany artifactClass CAPTURE_MANIFEST (:135-138). The remediation ledger (definitive-evidence-lifecycle-remediation/ledger-source.json ET-DC-11 obsoleteRemoved: 'the post-seal CAPTURE_MANIFEST relabel') was applied only to continuous-capture.service.ts:164-171. (web-capture.service.ts:121-133 has the same order — outside this area.)
findings.expected: Class before the seal, as continuous does.
findings.rootCause: Partial application of the ET-DC-11 fix.
findings.remediation: Move the updateMany above completeDirectCapture in screen-capture.service.ts (and web-capture.service.ts).
findings.requiredTests: uc2-screen-capture.integration.test.ts: assert the manifest part is classed before bind (e.g. part updatedAt <= evidence signedAt).

findings.title: UC-2 screenshot PNGs and the manifest are never deleted from the device cache after staging or discard
findings.userImpact: Full-resolution screenshots of whatever the user captured (possibly sensitive) remain in the app cache indefinitely until the OS evicts it.
findings.securityImpact: Plaintext sensitive screenshots persist on device beyond need (app-private, OS-encrypted at rest).
findings.reproduction: stageScreenCapture (screen-capture.ts:121-195) never deletes frame.uri or manifestUri; review 'Discard' only dispatches RESET (screen-capture.tsx:238). grep deleteAsync in apps/mobile/src: only continuous-capture.ts:157.
findings.expected: Delete each frame after its durable PUT (as UC-3 does) and on discard.
findings.rootCause: UC-3 cleanup was not back-ported to UC-2.
findings.remediation: Reuse deleteLocalFileQuietly for frames/manifest after upload and on Discard/Reset.
findings.requiredTests: Mobile unit: stageScreenCapture deletes uploaded frame files.

findings.title: UC-2 'SECURE_CONTENT_OMITTED' is assigned to any frame failure and never to actual FLAG_SECURE content
findings.userImpact: Secure windows are projected as black images (no exception), so a black frame is uploaded as CAPTURED with no limitation; conversely a disk-full/IO error is reported as 'secure content omitted'.
findings.legalImpact: Limitation codes in the manifest can misstate why content is missing.
findings.reproduction: captureOneFrame: catch (t: Throwable) { limitations.add("SECURE_CONTENT_OMITTED") } wraps bitmap copy AND the PNG write; there is no detection of an all-black secure frame.
findings.observed: Limitation code chosen by exception, not by cause.
findings.expected: Distinct code for IO failure; SECURE_CONTENT_OMITTED only when detectable (or not claimed at all).
findings.remediation: Split IO errors into CAPTURE_INTERRUPTED/a new code; drop the claim that secure content is detected.
findings.requiredTests: Kotlin unit around captureOneFrame error mapping.
findings.runtimeProbe: Device: capture a FLAG_SECURE app with UC-2 and inspect the manifest limitations.

findings.title: UC-2 frames taken after a rotation are recorded at the session-start geometry and orientation, with no ORIENTATION_CHANGED limitation
findings.userImpact: Frames captured after rotating are letterboxed/scaled into the original ImageReader size and labelled with the original width/height; the manifest orientation is derived from the initial geometry.
findings.legalImpact: Frame provenance metadata (dimensions/orientation) can be wrong.
findings.reproduction: widthPx/heightPx read once in beginProjection (:182-187); ImageReader/VirtualDisplay sized once (:200-211); each FrameOut uses the same widthPx/heightPx (:245-252); ORIENTATION_CHANGED_DURING_CAPTURE (declared in index.ts:40) is never added by this service.
findings.observed: No display listener in the frame service.
findings.expected: Per-frame real geometry and the limitation when it changes (as the continuous service does).
findings.rootCause: Rotation handling implemented only for UC-3.
findings.remediation: Register a DisplayListener; resize the VirtualDisplay/ImageReader and record per-frame geometry + limitation.
findings.requiredTests: Manifest validation rejecting mixed orientations without the limitation (as for continuous).

findings.title: If projection setup fails after consent, the native start promise is never settled and the screen stays busy
findings.userImpact: When getMediaProjection returns null (or resultData is missing) the service calls finish("ERROR") before onStartedCb is invoked; the JS start() awaits forever with the button spinning; the STOPPED event is ignored because the reducer is still in 'intro'. For UC-3 the server session was already opened.
findings.reproduction: ScreenCaptureService.beginProjection :168-179 returns via finish("ERROR") without invoking onStartedCb; the module's promise is only resolved inside that callback (ProovraScreenCaptureModule.kt:164-166 / :154-156). An exception thrown by getMediaProjection (e.g. SecurityException) is not caught in onStartCommand at all.
findings.expected: Reject the start promise (or resolve with an error) on any setup failure; catch exceptions from getMediaProjection/createVirtualDisplay.
findings.rootCause: Start success is signalled by callback with no failure counterpart.
findings.remediation: Add onStartFailed callback wired to promise.reject; wrap beginProjection in try/catch.
findings.requiredTests: Kotlin unit with a null projection.

findings.title: iOS native module exposes 'stop' while the JS binding calls 'stopCapture'
findings.userImpact: None today (the JS frame API throws on non-Android before reaching native), but the parity guarantee the F5 fix established for Android is broken on iOS.
findings.rootCause: F5 rename applied to Kotlin only.
findings.remediation: Rename; add a parity test that parses both native files against index.ts.
findings.requiredTests: Source-contract test over Kotlin + Swift function names.
